messages:
kevin: FYI, seeing a rack-level network flap in us-south2 (az-b). Scheduler is repeatedly evicting GPU pods — attach failures reported after node reboots.
```
E0130 12:34:21 scheduler.go:412] attach: timeout attaching gpu0: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing
WARN 12:34:23 pod-attach: backoff 2m, surrounding logs show kernel NIC resets
```
kevin: p95/p99 gen latency up ~2x for the region, some tenants getting 503s on heavy bursts. No Pager yet but this looks like a SEV. :rotating_light:

sre-lead: on it. spinning up bridge now and paging oncall. please post a short customer status draft when we know impact.

oncall-bot: Bridge created: https://our-bridge/abc-123 (ops) — participants: @kevin @sre-lead @julian @maria. Pager sent to @oncall.

julian: root cause hypothesis: leaf switch NIC firmware hit a regression causing connection resets during driver reloads after kernel updates. we're seeing identical signatures across 3 racks, so likely a batched maintenance or automated kernel update.

maria: are we confident this is local to us-south2? can we shift traffic to warm pools in us-east1 while we triage? Need ETA for customer note.

sre-lead: confirm local to us-south2. mitigation plan: 1) drain non-critical batch jobs in region 2) spin warm nodes in us-east1 and enable routing policy to prefer us-east1 for new requests 3) enable model-variant fallback for latency-sensitive customers (smaller quantized variant).

support-ops: Draft status page for review — please keep short and actionable. Suggest copy below: 
```
We are investigating elevated error rates and latency for inference requests in the us-south2 region. Some customers may see higher latency or transient errors while we shift traffic and remediate.
Impact: partial capacity degradation in us-south2 affecting requests routed there.
Mitigation: routing to nearby region and temporary throttling of non-essential workloads.
ETA: preliminary stabilization expected within ~45 minutes; full recovery TBD.
Updates: will follow every 30 minutes or when there is a material change.
```

sre-lead: edit: swap "nearby region" -> "us-east1 warm pool" and add "no data loss" line. Approved.

kevin: deploying routing change now — `kubectl apply -f routing/us-south2-shift.yaml` (will prefer us-east1, max 30% cross-region for controlled testing).
deploy-bot: rollout started: routing/us-south2-shift @kevin — canary 10% -> 30% over 5m per policy.

julian: parallel action: disable automated kernel rolling in affected AZs, collect NIC dump and driver logs, and prepare to roll back the firmware if confirmed.

maria: customer comm approved. support-ops, please post the status page and pin to the incident channel. Also prepare a short DM template for tenants with reserved capacity.

support-ops: posted status: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/2300001234 — DM template ready.

finance-liaison: note — cross-region routing will incur egress costs. please log affected customers for cost reconciliation; we'll evaluate absorbing vs pass-through.

sre-lead: agreed — prioritize availability for production tiers. logging owners now.

kevin: quick check: after initial shift we see request success rate in us-south2 improve by ~30% and overall latency trending down. still seeing pod attach retries, but traffic pressure reduced.

sre-lead: next steps: 1) continue routing canary to 30% then 100% if stable 2) isolate nodes with repeated NIC resets and cordon 3) bake hardware-safe rollback if firmware confirmed 4) post follow-up to customers with root cause once confirmed.

maria: ETA update: stabilization target now 45 min, RCA and timeline for permanent fix in 6-12 hours.

oncall-bot: Incident severity: P2 -> escalating to P1 if any sustained >10% error rate for >1h.

support-ops: posted customer update and filed follow-up ticket with account team for affected reserved customers.

kevin: logging all mitigations and costs in the incident doc: https://confluence/incident/2300001234. adding kernel/dmesg captures now.

sre-lead: good work. keep comms short, post next update in 30 minutes unless things change sooner. :thumbsup:
